slides.headline: Hours driving, then lifting parcels?
slides.sub: Where remedial massage fits for drivers and couriers.

slides.title: Two very different loads
slides.body: Long stretches sitting still, then quick bursts of lifting, twisting and stairs. That mix often shows up as tight hips, a stiff lower back, and a neck and shoulders sore from the wheel.

slides.title: What massage can do
slides.body: Remedial massage can ease muscle tension and help you feel less stiff after a run of shifts. It complements movement and strength work rather than replacing them, and the effects are usually short-term.

slides.title: Common areas to work on
slides.body: Hip flexors and glutes from sitting, the lower back, the neck and upper shoulders from steering, and forearms from gripping. Your therapist will ask about your route and loads first.

slides.title: Small habits on the road
slides.body: At each stop, stand tall and take a few steps before lifting. Roll your shoulders while parked. Keep parcels close to your body and turn your feet rather than twisting.

slides.title: When to see someone else
slides.body: Numbness, pins and needles, pain spreading down a leg or arm, or back pain after a lift that doesn't ease is worth a physio or GP assessment rather than massage alone.

slides.headline: On the road all week?
slides.body: Our remedial massage therapists focus on what driving and lifting load up, and suggest simple habits for the road. Book online — link in bio.

caption:
Sitting for hours, then jumping out to lift and carry? Your body feels both.

Drivers and couriers ask a lot of their bodies: long stretches still behind the wheel, then sudden lifting, twisting and stairs. Tight hips, a stiff lower back and sore neck and shoulders are common by the end of the week.

Remedial massage can ease that tension and help you feel looser between shifts. It works well alongside small habits: a few steps before each lift, parcels held close, and turning your feet instead of twisting.

Numbness, pins and needles or pain spreading down a limb is worth a physio or GP assessment.
